findings: External literature strongly supports purpose-specific, predeclared model evaluation rather than a universal hydrological fidelity threshold.
GW-R has useful authority for recharge sensitivity, uncertainty propagation and temporal-scale importance, but no transferable absolute recharge-error tolerance was found.

GW-D has useful authority showing system-specific recharge-to-head response and temporal sensitivity, but no independently authorized exchange/reversal tolerance or portable flux-to-head mapping was found.
SCI-P has measurement/product accuracy requirements and empirical profile errors, but these do not constitute independent process-model fidelity requirements.
Numerical water-balance closure, observation error and achieved model error are different concepts and were not substituted for application tolerance.
No new L4/L6/R8 or Reference validation response was exposed.

blocker.resolution_requires: A purpose-specific prediction requirement with threshold and temporal semantics established independently of Layer-ROM candidate performance. For GW-R/GW-D this may be an application decision endpoint plus an independently authorized groundwater response mapping.
blocker.cannot_be_resolved_by: Choosing a threshold from the frozen Layer-ROM error distribution or from generic hydrological goodness-of-fit conventions.

stop_criterion: 1. no defensible independent application tolerance authority
next_safe_step: Return only when independent purpose-owner/application authority supplies the missing tolerance semantics. Then freeze one purpose envelope and blind panel before any new response exposure.
